core_obligations: Record that the functor is faithful and fully faithful by the fpqc refinement lemma, so that only essential surjectivity remains (proof lines 9047-9049).

For a descent datum over U and a fixed member V_j of the target family, form the canonical morphism from the fibre product of two members of U over V_j to their fibre product over S, and pull the transition isomorphism back along it (proof lines 9050-9057).

Observe that the pulled back transition isomorphisms form a descent datum relative to the Zariski covering of V_j by the subfamily, and that each is an isomorphism between open subschemes, so that the pieces glue to a scheme over V_j (proof lines 9058-9066).

Glue the original transition isomorphisms to morphisms between the glued schemes and verify the cocycle condition -- the author marks this verification as omitted -- obtaining a descent datum relative to V (proof lines 9066-9071).
Conclude the equivalence, and in particular that schemes over S are equivalent to descent data relative to any Zariski covering of S (statement lines 9041-9043).
proof_roadmap: Full faithfulness by the fpqc refinement lemma (proof lines 9047-9049).
Pull the transition isomorphisms back along the canonical comparison morphism (proof lines 9050-9057).
Glue the pieces over each V_j using the Zariski nature of the covering (proof lines 9058-9066).
Glue the transition isomorphisms and obtain the datum over V (proof lines 9066-9071).
difficulty_reason: Let U and V be families of morphisms with target S and let a morphism of families from U to V be given whose components over a fixed V_j form a Zariski covering of V_j; the lemma asserts that the pullback functor on descent data is an equivalence of categories, and deduces that schemes over S are equivalent to descent data relative to any Zariski covering of S (statement lines 9019-9044). Full faithfulness is immediate from the fpqc refinement lemma proved just before, so the substance is essential surjectivity, which is constructed. Given a descent datum over U, one fixes a member V_j of the target family, considers the subfamily of U mapping to it, and pulls the transition isomorphisms back along the canonical morphism from the fibre product over V_j to the fibre product over S, producing a descent datum relative to a Zariski covering of V_j (proof lines 9050-9060). Because the transition isomorphisms are isomorphisms between opens, the pieces over this Zariski covering can be glued into a scheme over V_j (proof lines 9061-9066), and the transition isomorphisms over U glue to transition isomorphisms between these schemes satisfying the cocycle condition, which the author marks as omitted details (proof lines 9066-9069). The claim is H2: one comparison morphism has to be recognised, one pullback of a datum computed, and one glueing performed, and the only step left to the reader is the cocycle verification, which is routine once the glueing is in hand.
